question_text: If y = log(sin(log x)), find dy/dx.

mark_split.label: Differentiate the three layers in order
Write the ratio as a cotangent

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the layers you differentiate and the order you take them in.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate the three layers in order
steps.margin_note: First mark. There are three layers here, not two: the outer log, then sin, then the inner log x. Differentiate the outermost first and keep the inner part unchanged inside it.
steps.memory_tip: Count the layers before starting. Three layers means three factors multiplied together, so a missing factor is easy to notice.
lines: y = log(sin(log x)) is a function of a function of a function.
By the chain rule, differentiate the outer log first:
d/dx[sin(log x)] = cos(log x) · d/dx(log x) = cos(log x) · (1/x)

recall.must_convey: That the chain rule is applied three times: 1/sin(log x), then cos(log x), then 1/x.
accept: chain rule three times, one over sin log x then cos log x then one by x
differentiate the outer log first and keep sin log x inside
outer log gives one over sin log x, then sin gives cos log x, then log x gives one by x
chain rule moodu sarlu apply cheyyali, chivariki one by x
three layers so three factors multiplied

steps.why: The mark is for the chain rule itself, so writing all three factors before simplifying anything secures it even if the tidying afterwards slips.
common_mistakes: Stopping after two factors and leaving out the 1/x from the inner log x.
Writing the outer derivative as 1/log(sin(log x)) instead of 1/sin(log x).

steps.label: Write the ratio as a cotangent
steps.margin_note: Second mark. cos of an angle over sin of the same angle is cot of that angle, and the angle here is log x. The 1/x stays outside as a separate factor.
steps.memory_tip: cos over sin of the same angle is always cot, whatever the angle is written as.
lines: This working needs sin(log x) > 0, that is log x in (0, π), or in any interval (2kπ, (2k + 1)π).

recall.must_convey: That cos(log x)/sin(log x) is cot(log x), giving dy/dx = cot(log x)/x.
accept: cos over sin is cot so the answer is cot log x by x
the answer is cot of log x divided by x
combine cos log x and sin log x into cot log x
cos by sin ante cot, so cot log x by x vasthundi

steps.why: The examiner expects the compact form. Leaving cos(log x)/sin(log x) unwritten as cot is not wrong, but the cotangent form is the one the answer key carries.
common_mistakes: Writing tan(log x)/x by taking the ratio the wrong way up.
Putting the x inside the cotangent as cot(log x/x).

insider_note: Three layers, so the chain rule is applied twice, working from the outside in. cos/sin collapses to cot, and the final 1/x comes from the inner logarithm.
